key_insight: Foundational-NCA uses just 211,000 parameters to adapt to multiple medical segmentation tasks through genetic prompting without retraining.
clinical_relevance: Its compact size could support medical image segmentation in resource-limited settings, though clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Combines gradient-based learning with genetic optimization over a latent task space.
Uses a compact task vector to guide segmentation predictions.
evidence_signal: On TotalSegmentator, evaluation across 15 trained and 6 unseen segmentation tasks yielded average Dice scores of 84.5% and 60.4%, respectively.
watch_item: Lower performance on unseen tasks highlights a generalization gap; small parameter count alone does not establish deployment speed or clinical reliability.
paper_title: A 211K Parameter Foundation Model: Genetic Prompting in Neural Cellular Automata
